notes: THE LEDGER READS IN DATE ORDER. The General Ledger listed entries in the order they were posted, not the order they happened. An invoice dated in January but keyed in March printed below the March entries, and the running Balance column — whose only meaning is "the balance at this date" — was the balance in posting order. It also disagreed with the same figures in Reports, which had always read by date. Nothing about the ledger changed; the way it is read did. A LEDGER THAT SHOWS ONLY SOME PROJECTS NOW SAYS SO ON THE PAGE. A project leader sees their own projects and nothing else. The note explaining that was on screen only, so the printed ledger and the exported workbook — the two things that actually leave the office — were the only places that claimed to be complete, with totals that footed the part being shown. Both now carry the scope, on the page and in the workbook. WITHHOLDING FALLS ON THE SUPPLY, NOT ON THE VAT. Settling a liability that was booked at the full invoice figure — rent payable, an accrual, fees — could only be entered as "No VAT", which treated the whole VAT-inclusive amount as the supply and withheld on the tax as well. On GHS 12,000 including 20% VAT, 7.5% withholding took 900 where 750 was due: the supplier short by 150, holding a certificate that said so. There is now a treatment that says the amount includes VAT, and it withholds on the supply. FOREIGN-CURRENCY REVALUATION ASKS FOR THE CASHBOOK BALANCE. It asked for the balance per the bank statement and restated your ledger to it — folding every cheque the bank had not yet paid into the ledger as an exchange gain or loss. The reconciliation could then never be signed off, because the difference it exists to explain had just been posted away. It now asks for the balance per the cashbook, and says how to arrive at it. A CORRECTION IN PROGRESS SURVIVES A CRASH. Correcting a staff advance reverses the voucher, cancels the cheque and removes the advances, then offers a form holding everything it just removed. That form existed only on screen: a reload or a crash before re-entering lost it, and the advances were already gone. It is now saved before anything is deleted and offered back when you return. A COMPANY IS NEVER SILENTLY MISSING FROM THE GROUP TOTAL. If a company's books were mid-restore, the group overview left it out of the table AND out of the Combined total with nothing to say a company was missing. It now appears with a plain note that its books are not on this computer. BACKUPS. Changing the backup passphrase makes every earlier backup unopenable — they were sealed with the old one. The dashboard went on reporting them healthy and "proven restorable". It now says plainly that backups taken before the change cannot be opened with the new passphrase, and asks for a fresh one. The off-site copy also writes its checksum into place before the file it protects, so an interrupted copy can never look like a complete backup. SETTINGS ARE NO LONGER READABLE BY A DEACTIVATED ACCOUNT. Every other table already refused; this one was missed. Approval bands, control accounts, tax rates and payroll configuration were readable by an account that had been switched off. SMALLER, ALL IN THE SAME DIRECTION. A re-dated draft moves to the right accounting period instead of becoming impossible to post. A retry after correcting a date posts on the corrected date, not the first one. Undoing and re-recording a deposit no longer leaves a second, unclearable entry in the reconciliation. Correcting the same cheque twice is refused, with instructions, rather than quietly erasing a month. Opening balances and the bank reconciliation now refuse to proceed when a check cannot be completed, instead of treating "could not read" as "nothing there". HOW THIS RELEASE WAS CHECKED. Forty-three findings were raised by independent reviewers and each was put to two more, working separately, whose job was to disprove it. Thirty-three stood and all thirty-three are fixed; six were disproved and one more was withdrawn on closer reading. Five automated guards were found to have stopped guarding — one of them switched off by a change made the same day — and each was repaired and then deliberately broken to prove it now fails. The finished build was driven through a month of ordinary work and its trial balance read back off the screen.
